title: Exact tensor and two-target double-Hom functors with specified signed comparisons
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $L,M\in D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use $H(X,Y)=R\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)$ on the one-object ringed site [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], the direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], and K-flat replacements [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Put $F(K)=H(L,M)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K$ and $G(K)=H(H(K,L),M)$. Choose K-injective representatives $J,I$ of $L,M$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], and write $A^\bullet=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_R(J,I)$, using the Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex]. For a complex $U$ and target complex $V$, denote by $s^V_{U,m}:\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U[m],V)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,V)[-m]$ the signed comparison that reindexes source components and multiplies a degree-$q$ map by $(-1)^{mq}$.
Both $F$ and $G$ are exact functors of triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with coherent integer-shift comparisons $\varphi_{K,m}:F(K[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(K)[m]$ and $\psi_{K,m}:G(K[m])\xrightarrow{\sim}G(K)[m]$ having the following normalization on K-flat representatives $P$ of $K$:
$$\varphi_{P,m}(h\otimes x)=(-1)^{ma}h\otimes x\quad(|h|=a),$$
$$\psi_{P,m}=Q\!\left((-1)^m s^I_{\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P,J),-m}\circ\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(s^J_{P,m},I)^{-1}\right),$$
under the canonical derived representative identifications, where $Q$ is localization. For every chain map $u:P_1\to P_2$ of K-flat complexes, with cone $C$, the tensor-cone isomorphism on representatives is
$$\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_R C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(\operatorname{Tot}(A^\bullet\otimes_Ru)),\qquad h\otimes(y,x)\longmapsto(h\otimes y,(-1)^a h\otimes x).$$
It respects the cone inclusion and the negative projection defining the connecting arrow, the latter after $\varphi_{P_1,1}$. Exactness of $G$ uses the two contravariant triangle reversals, with precisely the comparison $\psi$ displayed above, including its factor $(-1)^m$. No boundedness or equality $L=M$ is assumed.

proof.text: Work on the one-object identity-covering site, whose module sheaves are precisely $R$-modules. Choose the stated $J,I$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $QA=H(L,M)$ and $Q\mathcal G(U)=G(QU)$ for $\mathcal G(U)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,J),I)$, for every complex $U$. No K-injectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,J)$ is needed: the target of the outer Hom is $I$. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $B\to A$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The exact functor $QB\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated] is $F$. For any K-flat $P$, the map $B\otimes P\to A\otimes P$ is a quasi-isomorphism, because tensor with the fixed K-flat $P$ preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs]. Thus $Q(A\otimes P)$ is the required representative of $F(QP)$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] with fixed first argument $A$: its second-variable comparison is $h\otimes x\mapsto(-1)^{m|h|}h\otimes x$, and satisfies zero and addition of shifts. The tensor-cone isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-homotopy-cone-signs], also for an arbitrary fixed complex $A$, sends $h\otimes(y,x)$ to $(h\otimes y,(-1)^{|h|}h\otimes x)$. Its inclusion equation and $p\phi=s^2_1(A\otimes p)$ imply $(-p)\phi=s^2_1(A\otimes(-p))$. Hence it respects exactly the negative connecting projection, with the displayed $\varphi$. Naturality in the fixed argument applies to $B\to A$; therefore these formulas agree with the exact derived shift structure in step 1. The same statements show that shifts and cones of K-flat complexes remain K-flat: shifts are covered explicitly; tensoring a cone with an acyclic complex is the cone of a map between acyclic tensor complexes, so is acyclic by [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] (the map between acyclic complexes is a quasi-isomorphism since all cohomology objects vanish).

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon(t)=(-1)^t$. The differential of [def-pur-hom-complex] gives $df=d_Vf-\epsilon(q+m)fd_U$ for a degree-$q$ map from $U[m]$. Multiplication by $\epsilon(mq)$ after reindexing is a chain map: both resulting differentials equal $\epsilon(mq+m)d_Vf-\epsilon(mq+q)fd_U$. Its inverse has the same sign, and it commutes with precomposition by chain maps. This proves the stated $s^V_{U,m}$ for every target $V$. Put $T_J(U)=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,J)$. For $g\in\mathcal G(U[m])^n$ and $f\in T_J(U)^c$, the inverse precomposition comparison contributes $\epsilon(m(c+m))$, the outer source comparison contributes $\epsilon(mn)$, and the leading factor contributes $\epsilon(m)$. Since $m^2+m$ is even, the displayed composite is therefore
$$(\chi_{U,m}g)(f)=\epsilon(m(n+c))g(f),$$
where $f$ on the right is reindexed to degree $c+m$. This proves that the prescribed $\psi=Q\chi$ is a natural chain isomorphism. Zero shift is identity. To compose shifts $m,l$, extraction of $l$ at $U[m]$ contributes $\epsilon(l(n+c+m))$ and extraction of $m$, shifted by $l$, contributes $\epsilon(m(n+l+c))$; their product is $\epsilon((m+l)(n+c))$. Thus $\chi$, and consequently $\psi$, has the coherent integer-shift law.

proof.text:
To obtain the mixed-target cone comparison without assuming $J=I$, apply [lem-sf-double-hom-cone-comparison] to the single auxiliary target $V=J\oplus I$. Its theorem permits every complex $V$. Finite biproducts give
$$\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,V),V)
=\bigoplus_{D,E\in\{J,I\}}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(U,D),E).$$
This is an identity of complexes: restrict a map to each of the two inner summands and project to each outer summand; the inverse adds these four maps. The Hom differential preserves each block. Every formula for $s,\chi,\theta$ in the cited statement preserves these blocks as well: $s$ only reindexes and multiplies by a sign, and $\theta$ only multiplies the cone-source component by $(-1)^{p+r}$. Restrict to the block $(D,E)=(J,I)$. With $X=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P_2,J)$, $Y=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(P_1,J)$, and $C=\operatorname{Cone}(u)$, it yields
$$\theta_u:\mathcal G(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Cone}(\mathcal G(u)),\qquad(\alpha,\beta)\longmapsto(\alpha,\gamma),\quad\gamma_r=(-1)^{p+r}\beta_r.$$
Here in degree $p$, $\alpha_q:X^q\to I^{q+p}$ and $\beta_r:Y^r\to I^{r+p+1}$. The restriction of the inverse of the four-block chain isomorphism is an inverse on this block, so this is a chain isomorphism, natural in $u$.

source.place: Tag 08JC (lemma-RHom-triangulated), reduction to the explicit same-target cone comparison by a finite biproduct of targets

proof.text:
The inclusion and negative-projection equations of [lem-sf-double-hom-cone-comparison] also restrict to this block. Indeed the double-Hom map induced by a source chain map acts on each block separately by two precompositions, and the cone inclusion and projection preserve the same four blocks. They give
$$\theta_u\mathcal G(i)=i_{\mathcal G(u)},\qquad
\chi_{P_1,1}\mathcal G(-\pi)=-\pi_{\mathcal G(u)}\theta_u.$$
The restricted comparison is exactly $-s^I_{T_J(P_1),-1}\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(s^J_{P_1,1},I)^{-1}$, namely step 3 at $m=1$. Thus no boundary sign has been suppressed. Concretely, $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(C,J)^q=X^q\oplus Y^{q-1}$ with differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Xx,d_Yy+(-1)^{q+1}\operatorname{Hom}(u,J)x)$, by substituting the cone matrix in [def-pur-hom-complex]. This is the first contravariant reversal; the second Hom and its $\theta$ sign perform the second reversal. The resulting connecting comparison is $\chi_{P_1,1}$, including its leading minus sign, as asserted.

proof.text: For any quasi-isomorphism $t:U\to U'$, [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] first makes $\operatorname{Hom}(t,J)$ a quasi-isomorphism, using the identity of the K-injective target $J$, and then makes its precomposition into the K-injective $I$ a quasi-isomorphism. Hence $Q\mathcal G$ descends to the functor $G$ specified by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The natural chain comparisons and their equalities descend as well: naturality for an inverted map follows by multiplying its naturality equation by inverses. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every distinguished derived triangle is isomorphic to a localized cone triangle of some chain map. Steps 4--5, which hold for arbitrary source complexes, identify its $G$ image, including all three arrows with the comparison $Q\chi_{-,1}$, with a localized cone triangle. Thus $G$ is exact in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Step 3 supplies its coherent integer comparisons, while steps 1--2 supply those of $F$ and the stated tensor cone formula. All constructions use only arbitrary complexes, finite biproducts, and K-flat or K-injective resolutions with no boundedness hypothesis and with independently chosen $J,I$.
